data.why: The repo ships a complete, ready-to-visualize ENAS run results directory (enas_example_run_results/) with 10 generations of chromosomes, results, crossover logs, config and search space files; EvoVis.py is invoked with this path directly, so no additional data needs to be written or staged.

goals: Review the hyperparameters and settings used for an ENAS run before digging into results
Explore the gene pool DAG to understand which neural network layers and connectivity patterns were searchable
Trace the family tree of architectures across generations to see which individuals were produced by crossover and mutation
Inspect an individual architecture's chromosome and measured performance/fitness metrics
Monitor how fitness and other performance metrics trend across generations to judge whether the search converged
Compare multiple objectives (e.g. accuracy vs. latency) via the Pareto-optimality plot to identify trade-off architectures

review.summary: The three phases filed so far (settings, search space, lineage with per-design metrics) are well grounded: ten sampled screens all matched their nodes, and the second agent replayed every task and feature. But the Run Result Plots page never rendered, so convergence trends, the Pareto trade-off view and the fittest-individuals list are all missing, and that leaves the stated goal of finding designs worth keeping unsupported; add that phase and its features before filing.
